key_insight: DiffVortex compresses the Biot–Savart kernel rather than the flow state, combining tensor-network acceleration with Lagrangian flexibility for moving and deforming bodies.
engineering_relevance: Its differentiable GPU implementation supports large-scale vortex simulations and gradient propagation through time integration for potential flow-design applications.
method: Evolve vorticity with Lagrangian particles and represent immersed bodies with bound vortex sheets.
Use quantics tensor cross interpolation to precompute tensor-network contractions for fast-multipole moment-to-local interactions.
Prove that kernel QTT rank r yields convolution MPO rank at most 2^d r, independent of grid resolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 6.7×10^7 particles on one GPU, validation on an impulsively started cylinder and inviscid elliptical vortices, and demonstrations with moving, multiple, and deforming bodies.
watch_item: Efficiency depends on compressible kernel representations; the abstract does not establish comparable performance for general three-dimensional engineering flows.
paper_title: DiffVortex: A quantum-inspired fast solver for incompressible flows
